details.note: No ': any' type annotations found in StationCard.tsx; test file uses 'as any' in two edge-case fixtures but not the component source

Component uses '@/' prefix (e.g. '@/utils/colorUtils', '@/services/theme') instead of the shorthand aliases '@utils/', '@components/', '@hooks/'. No relative imports present, but the specific required aliases are absent.
accessibilityLabel prop is set dynamically (line 93) and computed via useMemo including station name, line ID, and transfer info
export interface StationCardProps defined at line 31 with full prop documentation

llm_grading.feedback:
Readability (0.90): Code is clean and well-structured. Props interface is thoroughly documented with JSDoc. Helper variables (accessibilityLabel, transferText, lineColor) have clear names. createStyles factory function keeps styles separate from render logic. Consistent Korean/English naming convention follows codebase norms.

Architecture (0.82): Good separation of concerns with createStyles, useMemo-derived values, and a callback-based press handler. However, the task explicitly required '@navigation hook usage' for navigating to station detail, but the component delegates navigation responsibility to the parent via onPress callback. While this is actually a superior, more reusable design pattern, it does not strictly satisfy the spec requirement. Real-time arrival info (optional per spec) is also absent from the component.

Maintainability (0.80): Test file is comprehensive with over 30 test cases spanning rendering, interaction, accessibility, edge cases, memoization, and prop combinations. However, the test mock targets '@/services/theme/themeContext' and mocks 'useTheme', while the actual component imports 'useSemanticTokens' from '@/services/theme'. This mock mismatch would likely cause test failures when run, reducing confidence in test coverage claims.

Performance (0.95): Excellent optimization. React.memo wraps the entire component. useMemo is applied to styles (re-creates only when semantic theme changes), lineColor, accessibilityLabel, and transferText. useCallback memoizes the press handler. displayName is set for React DevTools. This is textbook performance optimization for a list-item card.

Security (0.85): No hardcoded sensitive values. Theme colors come from semantic tokens (no hex literals in the component). Safe null/undefined handling for transfers and nameEn. TypeScript strict mode prevents unsafe data flow. No XSS risk in React Native context.

feedback: StationCard.tsx is a high-quality implementation that follows project patterns well. Key strengths: thorough TypeScript typing with explicit Props interface, full accessibility support (label, hint, role, state), excellent memoization strategy (memo + useMemo + useCallback), and theme-token-based styling. The main deductions are: (1) imports use '@/' prefix rather than the required shorthand aliases '@utils/', '@components/', '@hooks/'; (2) the navigation requirement was satisfied via callback delegation rather than direct useNavigation hook, which is architecturally better but spec-non-compliant; (3) the test mock for useSemanticTokens is mismatched and would cause failures in CI. Overall score 0.851 — PASS.
